summary: This benchmark evaluates whether preserving 192 early-layer activation coordinates in a 238M parameter byte predictor mitigates catastrophic forgetting during domain adaptation to scientific Python packages compared to an equal-parameter late-copy control. The empirical evaluation rigorously adheres to a pre-registered protocol and reports a well-documented null result where the sealed architecture fails to show a statistically significant retention advantage on CPython.
strengths: Rigorous statistical reporting, including pre-registered effect thresholds, paired package/file confidence intervals, and explicit sample sizes.
Transparent reporting of negative/null findings rather than cherry-picking or exaggerating marginal differences.
Precise specification of hyperparameters, architectural dimensions (e.g., 238,269,312 parameters, 10 blocks, coordinate channel allocations), and adaptation budgets.
Careful experimental isolation between training datasets (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib) and held-out evaluation projects (pandas, NetworkX, xarray, seaborn, mpmath, joblib).
weaknesses: No verified supporting repository was attached to the platform ingest, requiring the benchmark to be classified under the text_only trust badge.
Evaluation was conducted on only a single training seed and matched adaptation budget, leaving open whether catastrophic forgetting dynamics diverge under longer training horizons.
The manuscript is extremely terse, omitting broader qualitative analysis of failure modes or per-domain variance across individual third-party libraries.
suggestions: Attach the source repository and evaluation scripts directly to the submission artifact rather than relying solely on inline markdown URLs.
Test under multiple distinct random seeds and extended training durations to verify whether retention advantages emerge under stronger domain-shift stress.
Include a breakdown of per-package bit-per-byte shifts across the six held-out external libraries to identify if specific packages experienced selective degradation.

claims.text: The Apple M5 Ultra is a hardware workstation platform capable of running local machine learning model training and inference.
Bits per byte (bpb) is used as an evaluation metric where lower values indicate higher assigned probability to the ground-truth target bytes.
The difference between CPython deterioration changes between the early sealed copy and late copy control was +0.00195 with a 95% package-paired interval of −0.00228 to +0.00710.
